guidance.procedure: Apply an exact predicate gate before deciding relation. For scope, identify stated content categories and any exclusivity term; generic “information,” communication media, access, or default confidentiality does not establish technical-only or non-technical breadth. For identification, require an operative mark, identify, designate, or awareness condition; keep oral inclusion separate from later confirmation. For agreement confidentiality, require language covering the agreement, its subject matter, terms, or negotiations. Name each exception category—independent development, prior possession, public availability, or third-party receipt—and never substitute one for another. Then make a separate whole-source membership pass: follow grammatical and numbered-list closure, include independently responsive definitions or exceptions, and exclude headings or neighboring procedures that do not establish the tested predicate.

For every lifecycle clause, record actor, act, object, trigger, coverage, duration, and exception. Decide return from the trigger stated in that same operative rule: termination or a source-defined event ending the transaction or relationship may qualify, but a request-triggered duty cannot borrow termination language from a separate survival clause. Decide survival only from an express duration or termination-effect rule, not from confidentiality, remedies, severability, or the agreement’s term alone. Decide retention by coverage and polarity: an express archival, backup, dispute, or legal-retention exception can permit possession; an all-information, all-copies, retain-no-copies, or backup-deletion command can oppose it, while a limited tangible-document return duty may leave it unsettled. Assign each span by function and collect every independently responsive rule without attaching neighboring mechanics.

First locate the exact operative verb: reverse engineer, solicit or contact, disclose, copy or reproduce, or use. Do not substitute confidentiality, ownership, access, recipient status, or a section heading for that act. Normalize actor, modality, object, recipient class, conditions, and exceptions. Keep employees distinct from outside advisers, consultants, agents, contractors, affiliates, and other third parties; expand a defined recipient class only when the operative disclosure rule incorporates it. A prohibition with a need-to-know, consent, or binding-obligation exception is conditional permission for the covered class, not automatically an absolute prohibition. For copying, distinguish permission or prohibition to copy from a rule merely governing markings on copies. Follow split sentences and every conjunctive condition through completion. After relation choice, include all independent purpose restrictions or recipient rules, but exclude recitals, definitions of status, remedies, headings, and adjacent clauses that add no responsive act.

Use two independent predicate gates. For compelled notice, first locate a legal, regulatory, judicial, subpoena, public-records, or comparable compelled-disclosure mechanism; then require an operative duty to notify, communicate with, or give the discloser an opportunity to object. A permission to disclose, a compelled-portion limit, or a section lead-in alone is not notice evidence. Scan separately for each mechanism and include every independently responsive notice rule, following any split sentence to completion. For no-license, require an express denial of a license, right, title, use right, proprietary interest, or intellectual-property right. Confidentiality, ownership, access, return, restricted use, or the absence of a grant cannot substitute for that denial. Include each independent denial and its grammatical completion, but exclude headings and adjacent provisions that merely describe ownership or permitted use.

Run separate relation gates for each target; do not transfer a clause or example across targets merely because they share this skill. For technical-only scope, require exclusivity: mixed technical, commercial, financial, personal, or business categories oppose “only technical,” while generic “information” or media language alone does not prove either breadth. For express identification, ask whether all covered information must be marked, identified, designated, or made known as confidential; “may be marked,” reasonable awareness, or marking only one medium is not an all-information requirement. For oral inclusion, require the definition or operative coverage to include oral or verbal disclosure, following any identification and later-confirmation conditions to completion. For agreement confidentiality, require coverage of the agreement, its existence, terms, discussions, or negotiations. Test independent development and third-party receipt as distinct exceptions; prior knowledge and public availability cannot substitute for either. After choosing the relation, make a second membership pass through definition lead-ins, grammatical continuations, and numbered exceptions. Include every independently responsive member, but exclude headings, examples of content, and adjacent duties that do not establish that target predicate.

For survival, require an express post-termination continuation, stated survival period, or rule that identified obligations remain binding; the agreement’s term, severability, remedies, or continuing liability for earlier breaches is not enough. A limited return duty may leave possession unsettled. Do not reuse return text as survival or retention evidence unless it independently states that predicate. Expand a defined representative class only when the operative disclosure rule incorporates it, and retain every need-to-know, consent, or confidentiality condition. After relation choice, cite all responsive acts and incorporated conditions, not merely the shortest proof.

(a) to keep confidential and not disclose to any third party, except with the written permission of the Disclosing Party, any part, or the whole, of any Proprietary Information disclosed to it under this Agreement;
(d) to restrict access to the Proprietary Information disclosed to it under the terms of this Agreement to those of its employees and officers who need to know the same for the Purpose.
